# Where the test documents come from

Every patient here is synthetic. No file contains real patient data.

| File | Source |
|---|---|
| `official-example.json` | The HL7 Europe Patient Summary guide's own example, `EPSExampleBundle01NoProblemsMedicationAllergies` (https://hl7.eu/fhir/eps/). |
| `minor-example.json`, `broken-example.json` | Copies of the above made invalid on purpose: the first drops the patient's name, the second also drops the Allergies section. |
| `rich-example.json` | A large German synthetic patient summary, used to exercise long lists. |
| `lab-example.json` | An example published with the HL7 Europe Laboratory Report guide (https://hl7.eu/fhir/laboratory/). |
| `mpd-example.json` | An example published with the HL7 Europe Medication Prescription and Dispense guide (https://hl7.eu/fhir/mpd/). |

They are the files in `provbana/examples/` of [Provbana](https://github.com/vadi2/Provbana).
The three documents in `samples/` (Andrea, Arne, Ville) are Provbana's scenario
documents from `events/nordic-hackathon-2026/samples/`, generated by a script there.

`test/golden/` holds what Provbana's Python summariser returns for each of those nine
documents; `tools/golden.py` regenerates it from a Provbana checkout. `test/corpus/`
holds every distinct call Provbana's test suite makes to its summariser and its document
type detection, with the result, recorded by `tools/capture_plugin.py` (a pytest plugin).
